record.context_brief: Krylov intersection and reducibility for Friedrichs operators
record.original_question: Characterize the Krylov intersection and Krylov reducibility for Friedrichs operators. In the bounded setting, the Krylov intersection is I(A, g) = K(A, g) ∩ A(K(A, g)^⊥); in the unbounded setting, when the Krylov subspace is defined, the corresponding expression is I(A, g) = K(A, g) ∩ A(K(A, g)^⊥ ∩ dom A). Krylov reducibility asks whether K(A, g)^⊥ is also invariant under A, equivalently whether A K(A, g)^⊥ ⊂ K(A, g)^⊥. The problem is to determine these structures both for abstract Friedrichs operators on Hilbert space and, concretely, for the classical Friedrichs differential operator.

evidence.quote: Definition 2.3. The Krylov intersection associated to given A ∈ B(H) and g ∈ H is the subspace I(A, g) := K(A, g) ∩ A(K(A, g)^⊥).
One then says that A is K(A, g)-reduced if in addition K(A, g)^⊥ is invariant also under the action of A, i.e., A K(A, g)^⊥ ⊂ K(A, g)^⊥.
When this happens, the generalised notion of Krylov intersection reads I(A, g) := K(A, g) ∩ A(K(A, g)^⊥ ∩ dom A).

QUESTION 5: To characterise the Krylov intersection I(A, g) relative to an abstract Friedrichs operator A acting in a Hilbert space H and a vector g ∈ H (see (2.8) and (2.9) above), as well as the Krylov reducibility of A (as in the spirit of Proposition 2.1). Or, at the concrete level, to characterise the Krylov intersection and the Krylov reducibility of the classical Friedrichs operator (3.1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$. For a bounded linear operator $A\in B(H)$ and a vector $g\in H$, define the Krylov subspace
$$K(A,g):=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{g,Ag,A^2g,\ldots\}\subset H,$$
and the Krylov intersection
$$I(A,g):=K(A,g)\cap A\bigl(K(A,g)^{\perp}\bigr).$$
For a (possibly unbounded) densely defined operator $A$ on $H$ with domain $\operatorname{dom}A$, suppose the Krylov subspace $K(A,g)$ is well defined (i.e., $g\in\bigcap_{n\ge 0}\operatorname{dom}A^n$ and the closed span of $\{A^ng:n\ge 0\}$ makes sense), and define
$$I(A,g):=K(A,g)\cap A\bigl(K(A,g)^{\perp}\cap\operatorname{dom}A\bigr).$$
Say that $A$ is $K(A,g)$-reduced if, in addition to $K(A,g)$ being $A$-invariant, the orthogonal complement $K(A,g)^{\perp}$ is also $A$-invariant, i.e. $A\bigl(K(A,g)^{\perp}\cap\operatorname{dom}A\bigr)\subset K(A,g)^{\perp}$.

Recall that an abstract Friedrichs operator on $H$ is a pair $(T,\widetilde T)$ of densely defined linear operators on $H$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(F1)] $\langle Tu,v\rangle=\langle u,\widetilde T v\rangle$ for all $u\in\operatorname{dom}T$, $v\in\operatorname{dom}\widetilde T$;
\item[(F2)] there exists $c>0$ with $\|(T+\widetilde T)u\|\le c\|u\|$ for all $u\in\operatorname{dom}T\cap\operatorname{dom}\widetilde T$;
\item[(F3)] there exists $\mu_0>0$ with $\langle(T+\widetilde T)u,u\rangle\ge 2\mu_0\|u\|^2$ for all $u\in\operatorname{dom}T\cap\operatorname{dom}\widetilde T$.
\end{enumerate}
The classical Friedrichs operator is the first-order differential operator
$$Au=\sum_{k=1}^{d}A_k\partial_k u + Cu$$
acting on suitable functions $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{C}^r$ on a bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, where $A_k=A_k^*\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb{C}^{r\times r})$, $C\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb{C}^{r\times r})$, and $C+C^*-\sum_k\partial_k A_k\ge 2\mu_0 I$ a.e.\ for some $\mu_0>0$.

Problem. Give an explicit characterisation of:
(a) the Krylov intersection $I(A,g)$, and
(b) the property of $A$ being $K(A,g)$-reduced,
both for an abstract Friedrichs operator $A$ on a Hilbert space $H$ with $g\in H$, and concretely for the classical Friedrichs differential operator above.
